CERTIFICATION_CONSUMED.rule: The certification is consumed as EVIDENCE and as a statement of defect, never as authority. BLOCKER_B1.defect_as_certified: The parent's K-1, ADJUDICATIONS.I, manifest P12 and manifest SEN-4 require the Vercel deployment id (dpl_...) to have been recorded BEFORE the deployment exists. Vercel assigns the deployment id server-side at creation and returns it from the create act; PR201 SB-4 correctly records it AFTER creation. The parent's contract therefore makes every future governed deployment inadmissible.
BLOCKER_B1.verdict: DEFECT CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT. The parent's contract is not merely strict; it is unsatisfiable.
BLOCKER_B1.root_cause_analysis: The parent correctly identified that CLASSIFICATION cannot distinguish a governed deployment from an automatic one, and correctly reached for IDENTITY instead. It then expressed identity in terms of the only identifier it had measured — the dpl_ id — without establishing whether that identifier could exist before the object it names. It could not.
BLOCKER_B1.the_invariant_that_must_survive: THE ACT is identified before the deployment exists. THE SERVER-GENERATED DEPLOYMENT ID is bound to that act immediately after creation. What must NOT survive is the parent's stronger and impossible form: that the deployment id itself pre-exists its deployment.
BLOCKER_B1.what_was_NOT_weakened: The requirement that a governed deployment be mechanically distinguishable from an automatic Git deployment is preserved in full, and is strengthened: this amendment adds two measured platform discriminators the parent did not have, and closes a copy hazard the certifier's proposed shape did not address.

THE_REDEPLOY_COPY_HAZARD.measured: Deployments with source="redeploy" carry the github* meta of the deployment they were redeployed from — e.g. a 2026-08-15 redeploy carries meta.githubCommitRef="main" and meta.githubCommitSha=dd36a4eca1 inherited from its source, not from any new Git event.
THE_REDEPLOY_COPY_HAZARD.derived_consequence: meta is COPIED by a redeploy. Therefore a nonce placed in meta does NOT uniquely identify one deployment: redeploying a governed deployment would produce a SECOND, differently-identified deployment carrying the SAME nonce.
THE_REDEPLOY_COPY_HAZARD.why_this_matters_to_B1: The certifier's proposed shape — nonce in meta, dpl_ id bound after creation — is correct in structure but incomplete. Without a one-to-one binding rule, a redeploy manufactures a second candidate that satisfies every nonce test. The amended contract closes this explicitly under ACT_IDENTITY_CONTRACT clause AIC-5.

ACT_IDENTITY_CONTRACT.status: SUPERSEDES the parent's K-1 and the first distinguishing property of ADJUDICATIONS.I.governed_cv1_staging_deployment.
ACT_IDENTITY_CONTRACT.core_invariant: THE ACT is identified before the deployment exists. THE SERVER-GENERATED DEPLOYMENT ID is bound to that act immediately after creation. The deployment id is NEVER required to pre-exist its deployment.

AIC-1_pre_existence_act_identity.rule: Before any governed deployment is created, the governed act MUST record an ACT RECORD containing: (a) an ACT NONCE of at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random source, (b) the exact Git SHA frozen and re-verified per PR201 AUTHORIZED_SHA_BINDING_RULE, (c) the intended deployment mechanism, (d) the timestamp, and (e) the human confirmation obtained per PR201 HUMAN_CONFIRMATION.
AIC-1_pre_existence_act_identity.why_a_nonce_rather_than_a_predicted_id: A nonce is the one identifier that CAN exist before the deployment, because the governing party generates it rather than the platform. Its unforgeability comes from being recorded before the fact, not from any property of the platform.
AIC-1_pre_existence_act_identity.the_property_that_actually_does_the_work: An automatic Git deployment cannot carry a nonce that nobody had generated at the moment it was created. This is a TIMING property, and it is why the act record must be written and timestamped before creation rather than assembled afterwards.

AIC-2_carrying_the_nonce_to_the_platform.rule: The governed deployment MUST be created with the act nonce and the frozen SHA passed as deployment metadata, using the CLI's documented -m/--meta mechanism, under the exact keys uellix_governed_act_nonce and uellix_governed_act_sha.
AIC-2_carrying_the_nonce_to_the_platform.measured_basis: `vercel deploy` documents -m/--meta, and the deployment record carries a populated meta object.
AIC-2_carrying_the_nonce_to_the_platform.why_meta_and_not_a_naming_convention: meta is part of the deployment record returned by the API, so the test is mechanical. A naming convention on a branch or a URL is not part of the record and is forgeable by anyone who can push.

AIC-3_post_creation_binding.rule: The server-generated deployment id returned by the create act MUST be captured immediately, within the same governed act, and written into the act record against the nonce. This is exactly what PR201 SB-4 already requires and is not changed by this amendment.
AIC-3_post_creation_binding.ordering: nonce recorded -> human confirmation -> deployment created -> id returned -> id bound to nonce. The binding step closes the act; an act whose id was never bound is INCOMPLETE and its deployment is INADMISSIBLE.

AIC-4_execution_time_verification_of_the.rule: Immediately after creation, the governed act MUST re-read the deployment record and assert that meta.uellix_governed_act_nonce equals the pre-recorded nonce EXACTLY.
AIC-4_execution_time_verification_of_the.fail_closed_branch: If the key is absent, renamed, truncated, case-folded or otherwise altered by the platform, the act STOPS. The deployment is NOT cited, NOT promoted, NOT aliased, and NOT redeployed, and the mechanism is re-adjudicated by a successor authority.
AIC-4_execution_time_verification_of_the.why_this_step_is_mandatory: This lane could not verify the -m round-trip without deploying. Rather than assume it, the assumption is converted into a checked precondition at the only moment it can be checked.

AIC-5_one_to_one_binding_first_bound_win.rule: An act nonce binds to EXACTLY ONE deployment id: the first id bound to it under AIC-3. Any later deployment bearing the same nonce with a different deployment id is INADMISSIBLE as governed evidence, and its existence is a GOVERNANCE INCIDENT to be recorded rather than resolved by choosing between them.
AIC-5_one_to_one_binding_first_bound_win.measured_necessity: Required by THE_REDEPLOY_COPY_HAZARD: meta is copied by a redeploy, so a nonce alone does not identify one deployment. Without this clause the nonce mechanism is defeated by a single click.
AIC-5_one_to_one_binding_first_bound_win.corollary: A governed deployment MUST NOT be redeployed. PR201 already forbids redeploying the failed deployment with build-cache semantics; this clause extends the prohibition to the governed deployment itself, for a different and independently measured reason.

AIC-6_corroborating_platform_discriminat.rule: In addition to the nonce, the governed deployment's record SHOULD be asserted to lack meta.githubDeployment and to carry a source value other than "git". These are CORROBORATION, never the primary test.
AIC-6_corroborating_platform_discriminat.why_they_are_secondary: The observed domain of source is not proven exhaustive, and this lane did not observe a CLI deployment on this project. A contract resting on them would rest on an enumeration it has not closed. The nonce's pre-recording is the load-bearing property; these two are a cheap independent cross-check that would catch a nonce mechanism that silently failed.
AIC-6_corroborating_platform_discriminat.fail_closed: If the nonce test passes but a corroborator contradicts it — for example a deployment carrying both the nonce and meta.githubDeployment — the act STOPS and records a contradiction rather than accepting the nonce.

AIC-7_what_remains_inadmissible.rule: Everything the parent's K-2..K-6 render inadmissible remains inadmissible, unchanged.
AIC-7_what_remains_inadmissible.explicitly: An automatic Git deployment is inadmissible as governed staging evidence whether or not it is Ready, whether or not its SHA is exact, whether or not its environment appears coherent, and whether or not the Vercel record shows a human as its creator.

PR201_COMPATIBILITY.rule: PR201 remains controlling for its own act. This amendment alters none of its semantics.

AIC-5's prohibition on redeploying the governed deployment NARROWS nothing in PR201: it forbids creating a second deployment, which PR201 already does not authorize.
PR201_COMPATIBILITY.sha_binding: UNCHANGED. AIC-1(b) cites PR201 AUTHORIZED_SHA_BINDING_RULE rather than restating it, and requires the same freeze-and-re-verify immediately before triggering.
